ev-goguryeo-tang-war:coord.reason: The record title and summary emphasise the fall of Pyongyang in 668; ours is Pyongyang. Wikidata's point in Liaodong reflects the 645 campaigns; both valid, curated choice stands.

ev-silla-tang-war:coord.reason: Ours is the Maeso fortress area (Yeoncheon/Yangju), site of the decisive 675 battle; Wikidata uses Seoul, 50 km away. Curated point is more specific.
checked: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi, Silla bongi (Munmu 15)

ev-mongol-invasions-of-korea:coord.reason: Ours is Ganghwa Island, seat of the resisting court (1232–1270). Wikidata uses Seoul, which had no special role; curated point stands.

ev-genpei-war:coord.reason: Ours is Dan-no-ura, where the war ended in 1185. Wikidata's rounded 35N 136E is a placeholder near Lake Biwa.

ev-mongol-invasions-of-japan:coord.reason: Both landings were at Hakata Bay (33.62N 130.33E). Wikidata's point lies ~54 km inland near Kurume.
checked: Thomas D. Conlan, In Little Need of Divine Intervention (2001)

ev-jikji:coord.reason: Jikji was printed at Heungdeok temple, Cheongju, in 1377. Wikidata's coordinate is the BnF in Paris, where the surviving volume is held, not where the event happened.
checked: UNESCO Memory of the World: Jikji

ev-founding-of-joseon:coord.reason: Yi Seong-gye was enthroned at Suchang Palace in Gaegyeong (Kaesong) in 1392; the move to Hanyang came in 1394. Wikidata's Seoul point is the later capital; state QID removed from event.
checked: Annals of the Joseon Dynasty (Taejo sillok, 1392)

ev-imjin-war:coord.reason: Ours is Busan, where the invasion landed in May 1592. Wikidata uses Seoul; the landing site is the better anchor for the start year, and route[] covers the rest.
checked: Kenneth M. Swope, A Dragon's Head and a Serpent's Tail (2009)

ev-donghak-peasant-revolution:coord.reason: The rising began at Gobu (Jeongeup, North Jeolla) in early 1894. Wikidata's Seoul point is not where the revolt took place.

ev-russo-japanese-war:coord.reason: Ours is Port Arthur (Lüshun), where the war opened in Feb 1904 and the major siege took place. Wikidata's 45N 125E is a rounded Manchuria placeholder.

ev-korean-war:coord.reason: Ours is Panmunjom on the 38th-parallel front (armistice site). Wikidata's point is in the Korea Strait near Tsushima, which is meaningless for the war.

polity-silla:to.reason: Silla formally ended when King Gyeongsun surrendered to Goryeo in 935 (Britannica: Unified Silla 668–935). Wikidata's 892 marks the start of the Later Three Kingdoms, not the state's end.
checked: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi, Silla bongi (Gyeongsun 9)
